causes.label: demand
causes.quote: High temperatures in Victoria drove higher than forecast demand

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Following the loss of the major transmission lines, several generation units tripped removing around 2,500 MW of low-priced generation in the region.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: At 11.07 am, Meridian Energy removed 60 to 66 MW of low-priced capacity at Mt Mercer Wind Farm due to unit maintenance.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: At around 1.10 pm, the Moorabool-Sydenham No.1 and No.2 500 kV lines tripped with reports that the transmission towers were on the ground.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding of capacity due to plant limitations and outages contributed to some of the high price intervals.

causes.label: constraint_violation
causes.quote: Not all these constraints could be satisfied, which led to them violating and being the major price setter for the 1.20 pm, 1.25 pm and 1.30 pm dispatch intervals.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Numerous constraints had to be used to manage system security leading to all interconnectors into Victoria being constrained.

causes.label: administered_pricing_or_intervention
causes.quote: When involuntary customer load shedding occurs, the price is set at the price cap.

interconnectors_named.name: Victoria-New South Wales (NSW) interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: Victoria-New South Wales (NSW) interconnector were at an average of 657 MW. This is less than half its maximum nominal capacity of 1,350 MW from NSW to Victoria.

interconnectors_named.name: Heywood interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: Heywood interconnector were at an average of 271 MW. This is only slightly higher than half its nominal capacity of 500 MW from South Australia to Victoria.

interconnectors_named.name: Basslink interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: Basslink interconnector were at an average of 356 MW. This is around 60 per cent of its nominal capacity of 596 MW from Tasmania to Victoria.

intervals.quote: The wholesale price of electricity exceeded $5,000 per MWh for 5 consecutive 30-minute periods in Victoria and 3 consecutive 30-minute periods in Tasmania on 13 February 2024 (Table 1.1).

peak_price.quote: the price is automatically set to the market price cap ($16,600 per MWh).

causes.quote: Temperatures of around 36 degrees was driving high demand.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Most of the remaining capacity was due to Origin Energy's Quarantine unit 5 failing to start with 75 MW priced at the price floor.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: the loss of the transmission towers on 13 February in Victoria were still influencing prices in South Australia during high demand periods.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Reduced imports across both interconnectors into South Australia and at times forced flows into Victoria.

interconnectors_named.name: Heywood interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: To keep the system secure flows were being forced out of South Australia and into Victoria across the Heywood interconnector.

interconnectors_named.name: Murraylink interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: Imports into South Australia across the Murraylink interconnector were limited to, on average, 50 MW. This was due to constraints managing the possible loss of Murraylink.
